respuesta.razonamiento: The architecture diagram shows Lagoon, an open-source application delivery platform by amazee.io running on Amazon EKS. Developers push code to a Git repository, which triggers Lagoon via webhooks on an EKS cluster. Lagoon deploys workloads to another EKS cluster (in hosting zones) running on EC2 and EC2 Spot worker nodes. The compute nodes interface with storage and database services: EC2 connects to Aurora (Graviton2 R6g), while EC2 Spot connects to EBS (gp3) and EFS volumes.
respuesta.nombre: amazee.io Lagoon Application Delivery Platform on AWS

edges.respaldo: Drawn arrow pointing from Developer to Git; 'create code and push that into their Git repositories'
Drawn arrow from Git to Lagoon EKS; 'In the Git repository, we have Webhooks connected to Lagoon'

edges.notes: Lagoon deploys environment to target EKS
edges.respaldo: Drawn arrow pointing right across partition line towards target EKS; 'it will go to the hosting zones... and then deploy everything we need'
Drawn arrow from EKS down-left to EC2; 'our base infrastructure is basically run with normal EC2 instances'
Drawn arrow from EKS down-right to EC2 Spot; 'we started our journey into Spot instances... for development or non-productive infrastructure'
Drawn arrow from EC2 to Aurora R6g; 'operator picks it up and provisions a database for you'
Drawn arrow from EC2 Spot to EBS GP3; 'workload that goes into an EBS volume because it's more specialized'
Drawn arrow from EC2 Spot to EFS; 'start storing your files in EFS because it's just normal assets'
